title: The Skill Koreans Rate Higher Than Talking

slides.kicker: THE HARSHEST REVIEW IN A KOREAN OFFICE.
slides.headline: **"He has no nunchi"** ends a career faster than bad work.
slides.note: It does not mean lazy, rude or slow. It means he cannot read a room — and here that is treated as a missing skill, not a personality quirk.

slides.headline: Nunchi is **reading the room**
slides.body: 눈치 is the read you take before anyone tells you anything: who is uncomfortable, what was meant, what to do next. The word is built on 눈, eye.

slides.headline: English has **no single word** for it
slides.body: Dictionaries hand you tact, wit, social awareness, savvy. Each covers a slice. None covers the whole move — read the room, then act on the read, without it being discussed.

slides.headline: At dinner, **nobody assigns the seats**
slides.body: Yet the seat by the door and the seat furthest from it end up with the right people in them. No one announces the rule. Reading it is the rule.

slides.headline: words of it are **spoken out loud**
slides.body: That is the whole design. A room where the arrangement has to be explained is a room where the nunchi already failed.

slides.headline: It is taught **before reading is**
slides.body: Korean children hear 눈치 있게 행동해 — act with nunchi — long before school. It is raised as a skill you practise, not a trait you happen to have.

slides.headline: "Order **anything you like**"
slides.body: Said by the senior at the table. Everyone then orders roughly the same mid-priced dish. The sentence was hospitality; the read was the actual instruction.

slides.headline: There is **a bill** for it
slides.body: 눈치를 보다 is to live under someone's gaze. It is the same reflex that keeps a desk occupied until the boss stands up, and it wears people down.

slides.headline: Fast nunchi is **a real advantage**
slides.body: It reads as attentive service, smooth negotiation, a host who refills your glass before you reach. The skill is genuine. The cost is that it never switches off.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
The worst thing you can say about someone in a Korean office is not that their work is bad. It is 눈치가 없다 — "he has no nunchi." It means he cannot read a room, and it is treated as a missing skill rather than a personality quirk.

Nunchi is the read you take before anyone tells you anything: who is uncomfortable, what was actually meant, what to do next. English offers tact, wit, social awareness, savvy — each covers a slice, none covers the whole move.

You see it at a dinner table where nobody assigns seats and everyone still ends up in the right one. You hear it when the senior says "order anything you like" and the table quietly converges on the same mid-priced dish. The sentence was hospitality. The read was the instruction.

It has a bill attached. 눈치를 보다 means to live under someone's gaze, and it is the same reflex that keeps a desk occupied until the boss stands up. Fast nunchi is a genuine advantage — attentive service, smooth negotiation, a host who refills your glass before you reach. The cost is that it never switches off.
reply:
One thing that did not fit on the cards: nunchi is not the same as being polite. Politeness is a set of forms you can memorise — bow, use the honorific, hold the glass with two hands. Nunchi is deciding which form the moment calls for, including when the correct move is to break one. That is why a foreigner with perfect manners can still be described as having none.

Does your language have a word for reading a room?

카드에 못 넣은 얘기 하나. 눈치는 예의바른 것과 다르다. 예절은 외우면 되는 형식이다 — 인사하고, 존대말 쓰고, 잔을 두 손으로 받고. 눈치는 그 순간에 어느 형식을 꺼내야 하는지, 심지어 언제 형식을 깨는 게 맞는지를 고르는 일이다. 그래서 예절을 완벽하게 지키는 외국인도 눈치가 없다는 말을 듣는다.

여러분 언어에도 '분위기를 읽는다'를 한 단어로 말하는 말이 있나요?
fact_check: '눈치가 없다가 가장 독한 평가' (1장·캅션): 직장 생활에서 널리 공유되는 서술이고 언론·대중문화에 반복해서 나오지만, 단일 통계로 확정할 수 있는 주장은 아니다. 카드는 수치 없이 '이렇게 받아들여진다'는 경향 서술로만 썼다. '커리어가 끝난다' 같은 단정은 카드 본문에 넣지 않았고 훅 문구도 'bad work보다 빠르다'는 비교형으로 제한했다.
'눈치는 눈(eye)에서 왔다' (2장): 표준국어대사전 기준 눈치는 눈 + 접미사 구성이다. 인터넷에 도는 'eye measure' 식 직역 어원 풀이는 대중적 설명이라 카드에는 쓰지 않고 'built on 눈, eye'로만 썼다. 어원 단정형으로 바꾸지 말 것.
'영어에 대응단어가 없다' (3장·캅션): 번역 불가 주장이 아니라 '한 단어로 대응되는 것이 없다'로 썼다. tact/wit/social awareness/savvy는 영한사전이 실제로 제시하는 대응어들이다.
'식당·회식 자리 배치' (4장): 상석·말석 관념은 널리 통용되는 관행이지만 업종·세대·모임 성격마다 편차가 크다. 카드는 '문 쪽/먼 쪽'만 쓰고 누가 어디라는 규칙을 명시하지 않았다.
'0' (5장): 통계가 아니라 수사적 장치다. '소리 내어 말해지는 부분이 없다'는 의미로, 본문이 그걸 명시한다. 수치 근거가 있는 것처럼 읽힐 문구로 고치지 말 것.
'글 배우기 전에 배운다' (6장): '눈치 있게 행동해라'는 육아 장면에서 흔히 쓰이는 말이다. 다만 연령별 습득 시기를 말해주는 공식 연구 수치는 카드에 쓰지 않았다. '반드시 몇 살에' 같은 표현을 추가하지 말 것.
'상사가 일어날 때까지 자리를 지킨다' (8장·캅션): 눈치야근으로 불리는 관행이고 보도·조사가 꼾준히 있었지만 최근 어느 정도 남아 있는지는 업종·세대차가 크다. 카드는 빈도 수치 없이 '같은 반사'라는 연결로만 썼다.
'예절과 눈치는 다르다' (reply): 사전적 정의가 아니라 해석이다. reply는 카드 본문이 아니므로 의견 서술로 두었다.
